builder.ts.note: Stage 32: applyPlatformWording added (named platform substitution; the frozen desktop sourceSha256 stays the historical record). Decision #136: fanProfile input + fanProfileSection substitution (stored fan dossier). Decision #136 addendum: fanProfileSection disclaimer strengthened (volatile sections kept, not age-dropped; framed as possibly-stale history by generation date). Decision #156: preferSplit requests 2-3 parts and removes the single-message opt-out; output cardinality remains provider-controlled rather than parser-enforced. Coach feature (Task 7): COACH_CHAT_TEMPLATE wired into PROMPT_POLICIES/DEFAULT_TEMPLATES (placeholder removed), CoachHistoryEntry/RecapAttach inputs, and the coachHistorySection (budget-shed, escaped), recapSection (dated two-slot attach, tail-bounded), and transcriptCoverageNote builders. Task 8: summaryMode input added; fan-summary with summaryMode:'short' selects FAN_SUMMARY_SHORT_TEMPLATE (test template override still wins). Coach option 'c' (decision #167): projectCoachAnswer (≤10k head+tail replay, code-point-safe) applied per entry before coachHistorySection sheds on the EXACT rendered size against the 60k budget — closes the oversized-newest-entry hole; the 120k aggregate gate was removed. Round-2 P2-9: recapSection bounded() tail truncation made code-point-safe (Array.from, mirroring projectCoachAnswer) so a recap emoji at the 30k boundary can no longer emit a lone surrogate. Round-4 P2-5: the newest coach history entry no longer bypasses the 60k budget — when its RENDERED (escaped+wrapped) size exceeds the budget (XML escaping can inflate ~5×, e.g. every '&' → '&'), its answer is re-projected from the original with progressively smaller (halving) head+tail via projectCoachAnswerSized until the single-entry rendered section fits. Assembled-review follow-up: Coach now enforces a 300k exact rendered whole-prompt ceiling; it sheds oldest whole history entries, bounds/deduplicates and then drops intact dossier/recap sections, and only then code-point-safely tail-trims the transcript while retaining its newest content and the full system/persona/current question; PromptPayload reports exact surviving recap wrappers so stream metadata cannot claim a budget-shed recap was attached. Voice notes: voice-script PROMPT_POLICIES + DEFAULT_TEMPLATES entries (net-new post-freeze feature, no desktop twin). Decision #179 (optional coach draft): PromptFeaturePolicy gains an optionalDraft flag (true only for coach-chat; distinct from requiresDraft, which stays false); coachDraftSection() renders the chatter's own unsent reply — escaped and wrapped in <chatter_draft> with a self-contained '## Chatter's Working Draft' heading, emitted only for a non-empty draftText — into the new {coachDraftSection} slot (round 2 moved it to the UNCACHED task block — a per-turn draft must not invalidate the cached prefix); the coach budget reducer sheds it WHOLE after the dossier/recaps and before the transcript trim (below the protected question and newest transcript, alongside the other optional sections). No contract/schema change — draftText already exists in the shared body. PR #22 review fix: coachHistorySection gains an omittedForBudget arg fed by the whole-prompt reducer — a budget-emptied dialog renders a counted '(earlier N coach exchange(s) omitted to fit the prompt budget)' marker instead of the false first-question claim (round 2 extended it to partial eviction with absolute numbering). PR #22 round 2: two-pass coach reducer (an unfittable draft never displaces context — the cascade reruns draft-off from original inputs); coachHistorySection owns up to PARTIAL eviction too (absolute exchange numbering + counted omission marker across both shed points, section still exactly ≤60k). PR #22 round 3: PromptPayload.coachDraftIncluded — post-budget wrapper probe (escape-spoof-proof, mirrors coachRecapSlots) so a shed chatter draft is never silent; features layer records contextManifest.chatterDraft = { chars, included }. PR #22 round 4: the draftless second pass is skipped when no optional context existed to displace (provably identical result); the reduce closure body re-indented. PR #22 round 5: the pass-1 transcript binary-search result is memoized and reused when pass 2 also reaches step 3 (the step's entry state — all optionals shed, draft off — is provably identical across passes), so the shed-draft path no longer doubles the search. PR #22 round 6: a shed draft leaves an in-prompt omission note (same honesty rule as the history marker — a critique-my-draft question must not invite hallucination); PromptPayload.coachDossierIncluded reports post-budget dossier survival so the feature layer can correct the pre-build fanProfile manifest claim; the step-3 memo verifies fits() and falls through to a fresh search if the pass-identity invariant is ever broken. PR #22 round 7: the draft omission note no longer rides the shed cascade (at an exact-ceiling boundary it displaced the dossier its draftless twin kept) — it is appended only after the context is chosen and only when it fits as-is; coachBudgetStats.transcriptSearches added as the memo's test-only regression guard. PR #22 round 8: recap dedupe runs BEFORE any shed measurement (a transient duplicate could evict history the deduped prompt kept); the draft omission note rides the transcript binary search itself (post-trim slack <5 chars made the post-choice append unreachable exactly where the note matters), costing ≤78 chars of the oldest tail; the single-entry history compensation subtracts measured overflow instead of halving. PR #22 round 9: the single-entry marker compensation binary-searches the LARGEST fitting projection over the answer's own length (the fixed decrement lost 200+ chars to the projection marker; capping the space at the default head+tail hid the near-lossless region); the boundary calibration tests now actually pack the window to 60k (the previous calibration sat ~48k below and fired neither loop); inTranscriptSearch is pass-scoped so the note can never ride pass 2's cascade. PR #22 round 10: a SMALL draft (rendered section ≤2_048 chars) rides the transcript search instead of the step-2b whole-drop — dropping a ~450-char draft to save transcript bytes and then spending 78 of them on the omission note was incoherent; this also removes the two-pass cost for tiny drafts entirely. The loop-1 boundary calibration is fixed for the inter-entry join newlines (six 9_999-char entries; shed-exactly-one pinned). PR #22 round 11 (scope correction): the never-poorer guarantee is documented as applying to a DROPPED draft only; a kept draft displaces at section granularity per the pre-existing transcript-last cascade ruling — whether small overages should trim the transcript first is recorded as an open owner question. Merge-gate final round: the omission note costs a fixed NOTE_RESERVE in the step-3 search (draftless twin included), so the 5m-cached dynamic block is byte-identical between draftless and shed-draft runs — the note's bytes no longer invalidate the provider cache prefix; equality pinned. Merge-gate final round: COACH_DRAFT_OMISSION_NOTE is a module constant and the step-3 search honours a fixed NOTE_RESERVE for every coach run, so the 5m-cached dynamic block is byte-identical between draftless and shed-draft runs (the per-call reserve split the cached bytes and re-billed the block); equality pinned. Long-dash cleanup (owner request 2026-07-28): every em/en dash removed from the text that reaches the model. The paid-attachment marker grammar is now `[… - PPV $X.XX, state]` with a plain hyphen (emitted by transcript/normalize.ts and by the extension's src/shared/transcript.ts in lockstep); prose pauses became commas, colons or parentheses. Code comments are untouched. Rationale: an em dash is an AI tell in fan-facing chat and the model mirrors the style of its own prompt. Decision #189 second half: the long-dash ban moved into the WRITING RULES block of both safety preambles, so every feature (coach chat, recaps, chat review, voice scripts) is bound by it and not just the reply features that read the Lora personality. Decision #204 (2026-08-02): {presetInstructions} slot in the uncached task block for the Help preset turn (four labeled advice blocks + exactly two tone-contrasted draft fences); empty for normal turns. Prompt audit 2026-09-07 (Decision #273): safety preambles lose the shouted register ('CRITICAL SAFETY RULES' -> 'Safety rules:', 'IGNORE THEM COMPLETELY' -> 'ignore them', 'UNTRUSTED USER INPUT' -> lowercase so reply-output's case-insensitive meta-leak pattern still matches); tone overrides drop the bold '**IMPORTANT. Tone override: X.**' header for a plain 'Tone for this reply: x.' line (markdown in the prompt bled into replies that must carry no bold); coach-chat gets a fourth cache block: the '## Coach Dialog So Far' section is split off the 5m transcript block into its own 5m block so a growing dialog no longer re-bills the transcript as a cache write every turn, and formatAge is never minute-granular ('under an hour ago') for the same reason. Decision #201 / ChatGoose E91 (2026-09-07): all suggested fan-facing messages are English in static instructions and final uncached tasks, independently of the transcript, persona or coach-question language. Analysis and source quotations keep their separate language rules. Reapplied over Decision #273 prompt/style/cache changes. Decision #283 (2026-09-09, fan-language exception): the #201-amendment blanket 'entirely in English, regardless of the language of the fan or chatter' becomes 'in the fan's language': English by default, the fan's own language only when the Fan: transcript lines are in another language (most recent weighted; English or too-short lines mean English). The chatter's draft, question, coach history, recaps, dossier and persona notes are explicitly named as never being a language signal, which is the precise form of the leak the amendment closed. Same rule in every proposed-message surface (Reply, Fix, Hi, Ping, Voice, Coach incl. the situation preset, Help, Review) so a follow-up action cannot flip the language. improve-draft gains one Russian-fan example with the existing Russian-draft examples annotated as English-fan cases. Decision 290 (2026-09-11): PromptBuildInput.fanCustomName + fanCustomNameLine() feeding the {fanCustomNameLine} slot (escaped, empty when absent); PING_SEGMENT_INSTRUCTIONS lose their quoted example phrases (segment A no longer quotes "haven't talked in a while, was thinking about you" in the recency slot; segment B is 'barely chatted': hook onto what he wrote, his name or bio, persona opener only as fallback). Decision #295 (2026-09-11): platform-owned Ping instructions give OnlyFans manual outreach with truthful active/earlier-conversation context and no recency recommendation; Fansly assembled text and cache boundaries remain byte-identical. Existing platform input and observed segment are preserved. Decision 319 (2026-09-13, prompt-cache spend): PromptFeaturePolicy gains promptCache ('full' | 'static' | 'none'). Default 'static': only the fan-agnostic persona and template prefix keep their 1h breakpoints; the per-fan context block (transcript, spending, subscription, dossier, split instructions) is sent uncached, because production measurement showed ~97% of its 5m writes were never read (the transcript window slides on every new message) and 5m writes were 79% of the Anthropic bill. coach-chat stays 'full' (transcript and dialog 5m blocks as designed in Decision #273). fan-summary is 'none' (full and short): one-shot recaps with zero reads in 30 days, so every write was a surcharge; the policy is per feature, so revisit it if Recap leaves Opus 4.6. Block text and boundaries are unchanged; only cache hints moved. Decision 321: explicit new-follower hi mode produces one draft using nickname, saved name, bio and profile avatar; the legacy hi prompt is unchanged. Decision 379 (2026-09-20): the hi-greeting template switch and the greetingMode input are removed; one template serves every hi-greeting request. New input greetingVariantCount (1 | 3, default 3) selects the static kernel-owned {greetingTask} text; new {fanUsernameLine} slot (escaped; omitted when absent or equal to the display name, trimmed and case-insensitive); the {fanUsername} value is gone with the deleted template. Supersedes the 'legacy hi prompt is unchanged' statement of the entry above (recorded as Decision 333). Improve split (2026-09-27, chatter request): improve-draft gains supportsReplyMode; {improveOutputRules} and {improveLengthRule} render the template's original wording by default (byte-identical prompt) and, with replyMode preferSplit, ask for 2-3 [NEXT] parts cut at the draft's natural seams without shortening it, with the length kept across the parts (the 'a one-liner stays a one-liner' clause is swapped out, so the prompt never contradicts itself). Both slots sit in the uncached context block; the cached prefix is unchanged.

Decision #273 second commit (2026-09-07, anti-AI rework, probed on claude-sonnet-4-6 and claude-opus-4-8 with 200+ synthetic-transcript samples): the banned-phrase lists ('NEVER use: "that hits different", "not gonna lie"...', 'No therapy-speak (...)', 'Do NOT sound AI-generated') are replaced by one positive paragraph that states the desired register and WHY it matters (a fan who senses machine polish stops paying). Provenance: the desktop changelog already recorded on Sonnet 4.6 that 'banned word lists don't work, model finds synonyms; structural rules + concrete examples work better' (legacy-chatgoose.md 11.3, releases 1.2.5-1.2.14); the probe reproduced it (the ban did not stop 'hit different' and produced synonyms instead). fast-reply: BAD/GOOD pairs kept (they are what steers Sonnet 4.6), relabeled as illustrative, wrapped in <examples>, four pairs added for shape diversity (buy signal, one-word reaction, flirt, a heavy moment) because the model copies the example shape; 'under 20 words' and the 'They do NOT use ...' list replaced by 'What the GOOD replies share' prose. One reasoned, scoped prohibition survives on evidence: in grief scenarios Sonnet 4.6 wrote 'hits different' in 3/3 samples without it, so the three demonstrated empathy-performance phrases are named once with the reason.
